text: At 65’, Kingsmoor FC implemented a tactical shift to a higher press (PPDA from 8.5 to 7.9) and increased directness (from 0.5 to 0.65), raising their defensive line height slightly (0.5 to 0.62) as a pressing trigger to recover possession quickly and accelerate forward transitions[#1187]. This approach sought to exploit width and crossing from their 4-4-2 while compressing Westport Albion’s buildup, but resulted in a reduction of possession (57.6% down to 51.6%) and a doubling of high turnovers (2 to 4), indicating vulnerability to counter-press and rest-defence mechanisms by Albion’s direct vertical passing[#1187]. Despite Westport Albion’s xG dropping from 0.73 to 0.58 post-shift, Kingsmoor FC did not increase their own shot volume or xG, suggesting the pressing and overload strategy had not yet created sufficient progressive passes or box penetrations within the 15-minute window[#1187].
